description: Committees can approve spending under $2,000.

New detailed budget process for advisory committees.
Standardized spending rules and bylaw changes coming.

chips.text: Recommended to Council

Five city council advisory committees are directly affected.

description: Upholds denial for Iranian Cultural Association flag raising.
City policy restricts flags of other countries at City Hall.
Committee concerned about setting precedent for flag exemptions.

chips.text: Approved
Councillor Pierce raised concerns about setting a precedent for bylaw exemptions.
The Saskatoon Iranian community appealed the flag raising denial.
Administration confirmed decision could set precedent for alternate country flags.
Iranian Cultural Association called the flag a cultural symbol of solidarity.

speakers.name: Pooyan Arab
speakers.summary: Registered to speak on: Sask Iranian Cultural Assoc
said: The flag is a cultural symbol, not an existing country's flag.
It's a gesture of human solidarity, not a political statement.
Other Canadian cities have approved similar flag requests.

description: Committee recommends new criteria to prioritize city programs.
Criteria will guide future budget decisions for city services.
Includes legal mandates, strategic alignment, and equity.

chips.text: Recommended
Councillors questioned the subjectivity, administrative workload
This is the first year implementing priority-based budgeting for the city.
Estimated extra administrative hours for the new budgeting process remain unquantified.
Councillor Davies will not support changes
New criteria include assessing programs' impact on underserved populations and equity.
Criteria include assessing programs' impact on environmental integrity and resilience.
Administration does not anticipate asking for additional resources for this budgeting process.

description: Recommends endorsing National Urban Park vision, governance, and provisional boundary.
Boundary subject to future refinements and public engagement.
Administration to support designation agreement, subject to federal funding.

chips.text: Recommended
Saskatoon Land Director preferred adding land to park later, not taking it out now.
Administration warned changing provisional boundaries now could jeopardize federal funding.
Saskatoon's model with local partners leading is unique for National Urban Parks.
Councillor Dubois felt her question about current Swale boundary changes was unanswered.
Swale Watchers and Wild About Saskatoon opposed reduced Swale protected areas.
Park vision includes cultural spaces for Indigenous teaching and revitalization.
Concerns raised that new boundaries exclude prime habitat for rare plants and birds.
Administration expects future boundary expansions to include more Swale areas.

speakers.name: Candice Savage
speakers.summary: Candice Savage, Swale Watchers, and Joanne Blythe, Wild About Saskatoon, expressed concerns about reductions in protected Swale areas compared to 2023 endorsements.
said: Proposed boundaries reduce protected swale areas endorsed by council in 2023.
New boundaries conceived behind closed doors, lacking rationale or public presentation.
Approving reduced boundaries harms park's ecological health and cultural significance.

description: Highlights urgent need for accessible Indigenous cultural spaces.
These spaces support identity, wellness, and reconciliation.
Future development will be guided by Indigenous leadership.

chips.text: Approved
Mayor Block questioned the need for spaces given Wanuskewin
Many questions remain regarding site locations, governance, and funding for cultural spaces.
Elder Linda Young and Shirley Isbister advocated for cultural spaces for healing and identity.
Cultural spaces are essential for Indigenous health, identity, belonging
Cultural spaces are connected to land, water, harvesting, traditional medicines
Staff committed to further engagement, refining locations, and exploring governance models.

speakers.name: Linda Young
speakers.summary: Registered to speak on: Indigenous Cultural Spaces
said: Longing for land and ceremony heals wounded souls for Indigenous people.
Need dedicated, accessible cultural spaces for youth learning from elders.
Current spaces inadequate for sacred fires during wakes and funerals.

speakers.name: Shirley Isbister
speakers.summary: Registered to speak on: Indigenous Cultural Spaces
said: Cultural spaces are a way of coming home, honoring people.
Showcase heritage, provide learning for all children, all cultures.
Needed for wakes, funerals, Missing and Murdered Indigenous Women gatherings.
